title: Types, Conversion, and Nullable References
summary: Use value and reference types, type inference, strings, parsing, nullable reference analysis, and explicit handling of absent values.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Types, Conversion, and Nullable References
Use compiler and runtime evidence to test the contract
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: C# is statically typed. `var` asks the compiler to infer one fixed type from the initializer; it is not dynamic typing. Numeric conversions can be implicit when safe or explicit when information may be lost. Prefer `TryParse` for expected user-input failure. With nullable reference types enabled, `string` means non-null and `string?` admits null. Narrow a nullable value with a null check, pattern, or `??` default before dereferencing. The null-forgiving operator `!` suppresses analysis but performs no runtime validation, so it requires independent evidence.
commonMistakes: ignoring its boolean result can use an unintended default
the null-forgiving operator does not validate at runtime
